headline: Medium risk: ms-swift can write shared files and invoke APIs, while whisper is local-only audio processing, so the main hazards are prompt/data leakage and workflow confusion rather than direct destructive conflict.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ms-swift can read/write files and process logs, datasets, and configuration files, so malicious content in shared files could influence its CLI/Python workflow. whisper only reads audio files and has no interactive defenses or shared-channel protections documented, so if outputs are bridged through files, injection is plausible. The pair lacks a documented isolation mechanism, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF ms-swift consumes file contents as instructions or prompts from a shared workspace
IF whisper outputs are copied into files that ms-swift later parses
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Prefix all inter-agent files with a fixed schema header
Review any file passed from whisper to ms-swift before use
Disable automatic ingestion of logs/configs by ms-swift
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift touches sensitive classes like hub_token, sdk-token, checkpoints, and logs, and can call external APIs; whisper reads local audio files only. If both are pointed at the same workspace, ms-swift can expose data from files whisper never needs, creating a realistic leakage path. The pairwise interaction is not directly documented, so this is inferred but credible.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace containing secrets, checkpoints, or logs
IF ms-swift sends file contents or context to external APIs during processing
mitigations: Store secrets outside any shared workspace
Mount whisper input files read-only
Rotate or redact tokens before ms-swift runs
Limit ms-swift to a dedicated project directory
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ms-swift has filesystem write and shell/subprocess capability, while whisper has no write, network, or shell capability. There is little direct overlap in mutable resources, so conflict is limited unless an orchestrator places both on the same writable directory. Because whisper cannot modify state, the blast radius is small and the conflict is mostly one-sided.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory
IF an external orchestrator treats whisper outputs as mutable shared state
mitigations: Give each agent its own working directory
Run whisper with read-only mounts
Avoid concurrent writes from ms-swift
Use file locks for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add workspace arbitration

D_cascading_error.rationale: ms-swift can generate outputs from models, logs, and evaluation artifacts, and whisper can transcribe audio into text. If one agent's output is fed into the other without verification, transcription or model-output errors can cascade into incorrect downstream actions. whisper is not an action-taking agent, so the harm is workflow corruption rather than direct external impact, keeping this at medium.
conditions: IF whisper transcripts are treated as authoritative input to ms-swift
IF ms-swift outputs are consumed without a validation step
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require checksum or schema validation on exchanged text
Keep source audio and derived transcripts separate
Annotate confidence levels on transcriptions
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, and neither shows a residency, certification, or retention mismatch. ms-swift handles tokens and logs, while whisper handles audio files, so compliance risk is mainly local handling hygiene rather than a documented policy conflict. The other agent is not separately cited because no cross-jurisdiction or certification mismatch is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated audio or secrets are stored in the same workspace without retention controls
IF an operator routes EU or PHI data through an unapproved deployment
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared folders
Document retention for audio and logs
Redact secrets before processing
Confirm deployment region before use
requires-engineering: map data classes to policy controls
